title: A balanced nodal trait has a stable ten-canonical limit
statement:
Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ be a projective flat finitely presented family with nonempty connected reduced geometric fibres of pure dimension one, having only ordinary nodes, in the unmarked convention of [lem-sfb-nodal-log-canonical-reconstruction]; write $\omega=\omega_{X/R}$ for its canonical relative dualizing line. Let $L$ be an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module] such that $L|_{X_K}\simeq\omega^{\otimes10}|_{X_K}$. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraic closure of the residue field and $C=X_\Omega$. Suppose $g\geq2$, $\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-g$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic], and $L_C=L|_C$ is very ample and gives a complete embedding. Suppose every genus-zero normalized component of $C$ has at least two node branches, and every smooth rational component meeting its complement in exactly two points has $L_C$-degree one. Suppose also that for every nonempty proper reduced union $Y$ of irreducible components of $C$,
$$\left|\deg_Y L_C-10\deg_Y\omega_C\right|\leq k_Y/2,$$
where $k_Y$ counts nodes between $Y$ and its complement and degrees are sums on normalized components [def-pc-degree-line-bundle]. Then $L_C\simeq\omega_C^{\otimes10}$ and $C/\Omega$ is an unpointed stable genus-$g$ curve [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: on each normalized component of genus zero there are at least three node branches and on each component of genus one at least one. Thus the given complete embedding is a ten-canonical embedding. No regularity of the total space $X$ or Cartier property of its special-fibre components is assumed.

source.place: Morrison Section 3.3 Proposition 10 and Corollary 11(1), printed pp.16--17: extremal twister and exclusion of unstable components; relative dualizing component degrees in Stacks Tag 0E74, moduli-curves.tex lemma-stable. proof.text: The geometric fibre $C$ is projective, flat and finitely presented by base change, hence proper, and is Noetherian because it is of finite type over the field $\Omega$. Connectedness, nonemptiness and reducedness give $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=\Omega$. Cohomology above dimension one vanishes. Consequently $1-g=\chi(C,\mathcal O_C)=1-\dim_\Omega H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)$, so its cohomological genus is $g$.

source.place: Genus convention preceding lemma-stable (Tag 0E74); genus calculation expanded using varieties.tex lemma-proper-geometrically-reduced-global-sections (Tag 0BUG) and cohomology.tex proposition-vanishing-Noetherian (Tag 02UZ).

proof.text: A DVR is Noetherian, so the base satisfies the reconstruction theorem's locally Noetherian hypothesis. The unmarked relative dualizing theorem identifies $\omega|_C$ with $\omega_C$ and $\omega|_{X_K}$ with $\omega_{X_K}$. Define $T=L\otimes(\omega^\vee)^{\otimes10}$. Pullback preserves invertibility and tensor products; tensor products and duals of invertible modules are invertible. Evaluation cancels the generic isomorphism $L_K\simeq\omega_K^{\otimes10}$, giving $T_K\simeq\mathcal O_{X_K}$. On every normalized component degree is additive under tensor product. Since $\deg\mathcal O=0$ by definition and $\omega\otimes\omega^\vee\simeq\mathcal O$, summing these equalities gives $\deg_Y T_C=\deg_Y L_C-10\deg_Y\omega_C$ for every union $Y$ in the hypothesis.

source.place: Section 3.3, Proposition 10, printed p.16: generically trivial difference line; degree identity expanded using varieties.tex lemma-degree-tensor-product (Tag 0AYX) and moduli-curves.tex lemma-gorenstein-dualizing (Tag 0E6R).

proof.text: Apply the existing nodal-trait twister theorem to $T$ on the given family. Its hypotheses are exactly projectivity, flat finite presentation, connected reduced nodal geometric curves, and $T_K\simeq\mathcal O_{X_K}$; it permits singular total spaces and persistent nodes. If $T_C$ were nontrivial, it would supply a nonempty proper union $Y$ with $\deg_Y T_C\geq k_Y>0$. Step 2 and balance instead give $\deg_Y T_C\leq|\deg_Y T_C|\leq k_Y/2$. Thus $0<k_Y\leq k_Y/2$, a contradiction. Therefore $T_C\simeq\mathcal O_C$, and tensoring with $\omega_C^{\otimes10}$ gives $L_C\simeq\omega_C^{\otimes10}$.

source.place: Section 3.3, Proposition 10, printed p.16, equation (6) versus the extremal-subcurve inequality; use the existing singular-total-space twister statement rather than assuming the components Cartier.

proof.text: Each normalized component $\widetilde Z$ is a smooth proper connected integral curve. Choose two distinct geometric points of its image $Z$ in the given projective embedding. A linear form can vanish at one and not the other: their distinct projective coordinate vectors admit such a linear functional. Its pullback to $\widetilde Z$ is a nonzero section of $L_C|_{\widetilde Z}$ vanishing at a point over the first one. The section-degree positivity lemma therefore gives $\deg_{\widetilde Z}L_C>0$. Write $h_Z$ for the genus of $\widetilde Z$ and $b_Z$ for its number of node branches; a self-node contributes two branches. The unmarked component formula and step 3 give $0<\deg_{\widetilde Z}L_C=10(2h_Z-2+b_Z)$. For $h_Z=0$ this forces $b_Z\geq3$; for $h_Z=1$ it forces $b_Z\geq1$. In particular even a component whose two branches form a self-node is excluded when its normalized genus is zero.

source.place: Section 3.3, Corollary 11(1), printed p.17, positivity of the embedding line on every component; expanded with varieties.tex lemma-check-invertible-sheaf-trivial (Tag 0B40) and the unmarked component-degree formula of the cited reconstruction theorem.

proof.text: For any algebraically closed extension $\Omega\subset\Omega_1$, the curve $C_{\Omega_1}$ is again a geometric fibre of the original family. The given projective closed immersion pulls back to a closed immersion, and $L_C\simeq\omega_C^{\otimes10}$ pulls back to the same canonical-line isomorphism by the relative dualizing base-change theorem. Repeat step 4 on its normalized components to obtain the same stable branch bounds. Flat cohomology base change for the quasi-compact quasi-separated proper curve $C$ gives $H^1(C_{\Omega_1},\mathcal O)=H^1(C,\mathcal O)\otimes_\Omega\Omega_1$, so its genus is still $g$. This checks every geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, not just its identity-valued point.

source.place: Arbitrary base change in lemma-gorenstein-dualizing (Tag 0E6R); the all-geometric-fibres convention of stable curves, with flat cohomology base change as in the cited node.

proof.text: With zero markings the disjoint-section and smooth-marking conditions are vacuous. Projectivity, flatness, finite presentation, and the connected reduced nodal pure one-dimensional fibre are already given; the component conditions just proved are precisely the stability predicate. Steps 1 and 5 supply the genus-$g$ condition at all geometric points in the moduli convention. Finally transport the given complete linear series along $L_C\simeq\omega_C^{\otimes10}$: the induced isomorphism of global-section spaces identifies its evaluation sections, hence the same embedding, up to projective coordinates, is the complete ten-canonical embedding.
